chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Safwan, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
There is no harm in performing all of the rites without wudu (ablution), except for the tawaf, for in it there is salat (prayer). And wudu (ablution) is preferable in every circumstance.

key_terms.الطَّوَافَ: circumambulation around the Ka'bah during hajj or 'umrah
key_terms.الْمَنَاسِكَ: the ritual acts and rites of hajj being discussed
key_terms.صَلَاةً: prayer; here indicating the special devotional status of tawaf
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: ritual ablution required for certain acts of worship

ai.seo_question: Can the rites of hajj be performed without wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the rites of hajj may be performed without wudu (ablution), except for tawaf, which requires special care because it has the status of salat (prayer). It also emphasizes that maintaining wudu remains preferable at all times.
